title: Classic layout can delete a focus again (2.53.5)
author: optimize-avo
body:
Karsa's focus delete is archive-first — POST /focuses/:id/delete answers 409 `not_archived` unless the row is already archived. The workspace satisfies that by construction, since Delete only exists inside the archive group. The classic layout (Visibility V1-V3) puts Delete on an active focus and has no archive UI at all, so every delete there failed with a generic "Failed to delete focus".

useDeleteFocusLegacy archives on the user's behalf and then deletes, reaching the same end state the workspace reaches in two user actions. The workspace flow is untouched: useDeleteFocus and useFocusLifecycle still require an explicit archive first.

Deliberately not the permissive DELETE verb, even though it is one request: against a Karsa build older than the soft-delete work that verb still runs the old hard cascade, which deletes avq_focus_vs and avq_pb_prompts rows out of completed, frozen snapshots — measurement history that cannot be recomputed, erased with no error. Archive-then-delete 404s against such a build instead.

Optimism moves to the `active` query key, which is what the classic lists render from, and rolls back only when the archive step itself failed: once the focus is archived it really has left the list, so restoring the row would show a focus the server no longer measures. A delete that fails after a successful archive now says so rather than claiming the delete failed outright.

Also corrects the Prompt Book delete dialog, which promised it would "permanently delete all prompts, build history, and measurement data" over a soft delete that keeps all three, and was the last hardcoded-English dialog in that card. Translated across all six UI locales.

author: thefdisk

title: Stop false-positive errors on VS probe progress l…
author: optimize-avo
body:
…ines

The inferLevelFromMessage() classifier was marking every VS probe progress line (e.g. "OK 25 FAIL 0 SKIP 0") as warn/error because it matched keywords "SKIP" and "FAIL" without checking their counts.

Two fixes:
1. Early-return parser for "OK N FAIL N SKIP N" format — reads actual counts instead of keyword-matching (also prevents "OK 2 FAIL 0" being read as "2 fail" due to adjacent number from OK count).
2. Added hasNoSkipPhrase guard so "SKIP 0" / "0 skip" doesn't trigger warn.

title: [Release] AVO V2 Production
author: ikhsan-sr
body:
….62.0)

Release-line port of avq-sutra#257's content-opportunity work, backing the Archive group that avq-astra's feature/alex-work-layout-v2-release now ships.

- POST /api/client/content/opportunities/:id/restore — un-archive
- POST /api/client/content/opportunities/:id/delete — soft delete upstream; the row survives as a tombstone so the miner doesn't re-detect the topic, and a paid brief stays auditable. Archive-first, surfacing Ava's 409 not_archived unchanged.

All three lifecycle proxies (dismiss, restore, delete) forward orgId to Ava so the write is confined to the caller's org upstream too — Ava previously matched on opportunity id alone.

Written in this branch's route idiom (explicit uuidSchema guard, handler-as-second-arg) instead of the staging branch's schema-block form: the idParams and upstreamErrors helpers that form depends on do not exist on the release line. Same endpoints, same service calls, same error handling. The service layer cherry-picked clean.

Version 0.55.0 -> 0.62.0 (release line is at 0.61.0; staging's numbering would have been a regression here).

Deliberately NOT ported from the same PR branch: the focus archive / soft-delete / operator-restore commit (staging 0.56.0). Astra's release line archives focuses through the existing PATCH status route, not those new endpoints, and Karsa's release line has no focus soft-delete support at all (no deleted_at on focuses), so the focus /delete proxy would fail at runtime in production. Flagged for Alex rather than shipped.

Requires avq-ava >= migration 082 (the release-line Ava port).

title: Engine roster comes from the API, not a local catalog…
author: optimize-avo
body:
… (1.55.0)

WizardPlatformStep held a PROVIDER_CATALOG constant listing every provider and model by hand. The wizard intersected the API's enabled platforms with that constant and silently dropped anything it did not recognise, so an engine registered in Karsa later — Kimi (Moonshot), MiniMax, Qwen — never appeared here no matter how it was configured in Shastra.

- PROVIDER_CATALOG is deleted. The roster is the platform list from the API, which derives it from Karsa's adapter registry (Sutra 0.76.0, Karsa 2.151.0).
- Label and colour come from the API entry, falling back to the existing --color-plat-* tokens for engines that have one. buildSlot, the default-slot matcher and MeasurementSummary no longer consult a local provider table.
- Engines with no API key are filtered out of the picker: a client must not be able to add an engine to a paid measurement when it cannot answer.
- The model sent to Karsa is model_id, resolved server-side from the operator's vs.platform.{key}.model choice, instead of the first entry of a hardcoded model array. MeasurementSummary.resolveModel no longer invents a model from it.
- Pre-selected engines are unchanged: DEFAULT_PLATFORM_NAMES is a default SELECTION, not a roster, so a newly registered engine is not auto-added — every slot multiplies probe count and cost.
- VsPlatformConfig gains label/color/kind/usable.

title: Align Astra HTTP timeouts with Sutra/Ava budget (FE-only)
author: optimize-avo
body:
Astra aborted every request at the 30s axios default, but several hops behind Sutra have a worst-case budget longer than 30s. On slow paths Astra gave up first (ECONNABORTED, no response.status), every classifier missed it, and users saw a generic "failed" toast while the backend was still working — and retrying hooks re-fired the abort, duplicating expensive LLM work. This is a frontend-only change; no backend repo is touched.

- api-error: add isAbortError / isProcessingError + a `kind` field so client aborts and Sutra 504 gateway_timeouts are classified as "still preparing", not "failed".
- sutra-client: interceptor gives aborts and 504s a calm message; export AVA_READ_TIMEOUT_MS (55s) and AVA_LLM_TIMEOUT_MS (130s).
- query-client: retryUnlessAbort() — never auto-retry a client abort (duplicate-spend fix) or an in-flight 504; reused as the global default.
- Per-endpoint 55s timeout on slow Ava-backed reads (domains/:id/ava, ava/summary, org-dashboard, domain-brief, market-outlook, movements, account-insights, position, portfolio-health, market-pulse) so Astra no longer aborts before Sutra's ~49.5s avaFetch finishes.
- translate-persist POST: 130s override (Sutra already waits 120s, Ava 180s).

Known limit (BE follow-up): caption + content-translation GETs are capped at 15s inside Sutra (avaV2Fetch); on a cold cache they 504 regardless of Astra. They are now classified honestly; the real fix is async-ify or a longer avaV2Fetch budget on the backend.

title: Prevent XSS in Ava loader, activity log, and markdown …
author: optimize-avo
body:
…links

Three confirmed XSS sinks in the client portal, all rendering untrusted data as raw HTML without escaping:

- H1 (stored XSS): pickMessage() interpolated `vars` into developer-authored HTML templates with an unescaped replaceAll. vars.focus is the client's own focus statement, rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML in the VS/AS loaders — a focus statement containing markup executed for anyone in the org viewing the run. - H2 (DOM XSS): AvaPartnerDetail rendered activity-log `entry.m` (server metadata + SSE stream) via dangerouslySetInnerHTML. The `level` is already derived client-side, so the message needs no HTML — render it as text.

- M1: MarkdownRenderer copied markdown link URLs into href with no protocol allowlist, so a `[x](javascript:...)` link in LLM-generated draft content was clickable. Now allowlists http/https/mailto/tel/relative/anchor, else `#`.

title: Isolate job error/activity logs to the job (v2.175.1)
author: optimize-avo
body:
The Job Inspector "Errors" and "Activity" tabs leaked global logs from other jobs and domains, and rendered "Invalid Date" for system entries.

Root cause: useJobLogs called GET /api/logs?traceId=<jobId>, but Karsa's logs query schema expects snake_case `trace_id`. Zod stripped the unknown `traceId` key, so no trace filter was applied and the endpoint returned the latest 200 logs across ALL jobs/domains. That same endpoint also returns snake_case fields (created_at), so `new Date(log.createdAt)` was NaN -> "Invalid Date".

Fix:
- Switch useJobLogs to the trace-scoped endpoint GET /api/logs/trace/:jobId (path param parsed server-side), so logs are isolated to this job. This endpoint also returns camelCase fields (createdAt/traceId) via formatLog, fixing the timestamps.
- Guard timestamp rendering in JobInspector (mergeActivityItems + formatLogTime helper) so any missing/bad time shows "—" instead of "Invalid Date".

title: Explain why + effect on AS measurement partial ribbon
author: optimize-avo
body:
The degraded ("AS measurement partial") health ribbon showed only a title with no explanation, since the success path nulls last_failure_hint. Clients had no way to know why the measurement was partial or what it means.

- DomainHealthRibbon: when no backend hint is present, fall back to a localized run_state.{state}.body explaining the cause and the effect.
- Add run_state.degraded.body to all 5 locales (en/id/ja/ko/zh-TW): "This site blocks automated crawlers, so the score was measured through a limited fallback. The score is still valid, but its accuracy may be slightly reduced."

Hint-first ordering preserved, so blocked/failed states still show their backend-supplied hints unchanged.

commits.message: feat(domain): explain why + effect on AS measurement partial ribbon
